description:
FILED s507 (Fable, 2026-10-04), found while checking that a required file ignores its own `#!` line (s506f review).  A program's FIRST run under `pcl` differs from every later run -- the worst kind of flake to meet as a new user.

REPRODUCER (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s507/review/tmp/x/):
  t1.pl:   print "t1 loaded\n"; sub t1f { "f" } 1;
  q1.pl:   require "./t1.pl"; print "A ", (defined(&t1f) ? t1f() : "nosub"), "\n";
  perl q1.pl                      t1 loaded / A f
  pcl --no-cache q1.pl            t1 loaded / A f
  runpcl q1.pl                    t1 loaded / A f
  pcl q1.pl   (first time)        A f                    <- "t1 loaded" is MISSING
  pcl q1.pl   (second time)       t1 loaded / A f
Measured on the 618db500 extraction and on main 2e71d4aa: same.  The sub IS defined on the first run, so the file was loaded -- its output went somewhere else, or it was executed at a phase whose STDOUT is discarded.
SUSPECT (cheap discriminating measurement, NOT taken): on a script-cache MISS the driver compiles the emitted program (compile-file) and then runs it in the SAME image; the emitted `(p-require-file "./t1.pl")` sits in an eval-when that also fires at COMPILE time, when the compiler's output stream is muffled -- the required file runs there (prints into the muffled stream, defines t1f, sets %INC), and the load that follows finds it in %INC and does not run it again.  Measurement: `PCL_SHOW_SBCL=1 pcl q1.pl` on a fresh copy of q1.pl to see the miss path's command, then make t1.pl write to STDERR and to a file as well (`open my $f, '>>', 'side.txt'; print $f "x\n"`) -- if side.txt gains ONE line on the first run and STDERR shows the text, the require ran once at compile time with STDOUT muffled; if side.txt gains TWO lines, it runs twice (a double execution, the [[project_module_compile_load_double_exec]] family) and only the first one's output is lost.
WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE PRINT: any side effect of a required file's top level happens at COMPILE time on the first run and at RUN time later -- ordering against the main program's own statements differs between run 1 and run 2 (a `require "./config.pl"` that reads %ENV set earlier by the main program; a `chdir`; an `open`).  Check `do "./file.pl"` and `use lib '.'; require Module;` for the same split (the BEGIN-time `use` is SUPPOSED to run at compile time; a run-time `require` is not).
FIX DIRECTION: a RUN-time `require` of a file must not execute at the compile phase of the cache-building run -- either the miss path loads source (as --no-cache does) and compiles for the NEXT run afterwards, or the require form is run-time only and its prototype harvest (the reason it is visible at compile time: #681, `_extract_file_prototypes`) stays a static read.  Guard: a `Pl/t/script-cache-01.t` row running a fresh script twice and comparing both STDOUTs to perl's.
subject: SILENT WRONG, FIRST RUN ONLY (found by a s507 review probe, PRE-EXISTING: identical on 618db500 and main 2e71d4aa): the run that BUILDS the script cache loses the STDOUT of a `require "./file.pl"`'s top-level code -- `pcl q.pl` prints `A f` the first time and `t1 loaded / A f` every later time (perl and `pcl --no-cache`: always both lines)
